prompt: Mid-case: A hospital wants to cut ER waiting times. You've found that 40% of ER visits are non-urgent and could go to urgent care clinics. You haven't looked at ER staffing. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: ER staffing is the main cause of the long waits. Next I'd look at urgent care.
options.feedback: This claims findings the analysis hasn't shown. Summarize only what you've established.

options.text: So far: 40% of ER visits are non-urgent and could be handled at urgent care clinics, which would free a large share of ER capacity. We haven't yet looked at ER staffing, so next I'd check whether staffing at peak hours also contributes.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open and what comes next.

options.text: We've looked at the mix of ER visits. We still need to look at ER staffing, and next I'd check whether staffing at peak hours also contributes. The main finding so far is that 40% of ER visits are non-urgent and could be handled at urgent care clinics, which would free a large share of ER capacity.
options.feedback: The answer comes last. Lead with the recommendation, then support it.

options.text: So far: many visits probably don't need to be in the ER. Next I'd check whether staffing at peak hours also contributes.
options.feedback: It gives an answer but none of the numbers from the fact sheet to back it.

explanation: 40% of ER visits are non-urgent and could be handled at urgent care clinics, which would free a large share of ER capacity. A good mid-case summary states what is known with numbers and what comes next, without claiming findings that haven't been tested.

irrelevant_facts: The hospital has a helicopter pad.
